answer: A concrete sybil defense: every identity stores its attestation in a vault opened only by a fresh epoch-bound proof. The network demands a karst of provenance — a porous history where each claim settles on verified bedrock of prior accepted attestations. A clone farm cannot manufacture that depth; it must fabricate a lagoon of independent cross-verified work across epochs. The system rejects clusters whose provenance graphs show low branching factor or matching timestamps. Attacking costs one real proof layer per fake identity per epoch; reward stays capped.
